question: to the Commission Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy (Renew), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Manuela Ripa (PPE), Michal Wiezik (Renew), Sebastian Everding (The Left), Sirpa Pietikäinen (PPE), Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Martin Hojsík (Renew), César Luena (S&D) Subject:

Through its revised action plan against wildlife trafficking, the Commission has committed itself to promoting the adoption of a protocol covering wildlife trafficking under the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC)1. With the UNTOC Conference of the Parties (COP) scheduled for October 2026, decisive diplomatic engagement will be essential to achieve this objective. In this context, could the Commission clarify: 1.

What concrete diplomatic, political and technical steps it is taking to advance negotiations towards developing and adopting a protocol to UNTOC that addresses wildlife trafficking and other environmental crimes?

With other UNTOC Parties considering a draft resolution at the UNTOC COP to seek a negotiating mandate for a potential protocol to UNTOC, how is the Commission coordinating with EU Member States to secure a strong, unified and ambitious EU position?
What outreach and coalition-building it is undertaking with other UNTOC Parties to unblock outstanding issues and build the support needed to achieve a positive outcome in October 2026?

answer: (English version) to the Commission Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy (Renew), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Manuela Ripa (PPE), Michal Wiezik (Renew), Sebastian Everding (The Left), Sirpa Pietikäinen (PPE), Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Martin Hojsík (Renew), César Luena (S&D) (31 March 2026) Subject: Fourth Protocol on Environmental Crimes to UNTOC Through its revised action plan against wildlife trafficking, the Commission has committed itself to promoting the adoption of a protocol covering wildlife trafficking under the UN Convention against Transnational Organised Crime (UNTOC) (1). With the UNTOC Conference of the Parties (COP) scheduled for October 2026, decisive diplomatic engagement will be essential to achieve this objective. In this context, could the Commission clarify: 1.

What concrete diplomatic, political and technical steps it is taking to advance negotiations towards developing and adopting a protocol to UNTOC that addresses wildlife trafficking and other environmental crimes?

With other UNTOC Parties considering a draft resolution at the UNTOC COP to seek a negotiating mandate for a potential protocol to UNTOC, how is the Commission coordinating with EU Member States to secure a strong, unified and ambitious EU position?
What outreach and coalition-building it is undertaking with other UNTOC Parties to unblock outstanding issues and build the support needed to achieve a positive outcome in October 2026?

(6 July 2026) At the second meeting of the Open-ended Intergovernmental Expert Group on crimes that affect the environment falling within the scope of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organised Crime (UNTOC), discussions among State Parties highlighted significant divergences regarding the possible development of an additional protocol to UNTOC. As a result of these divergent positions, substantive discussions on the potential scope and content of a protocol, whether limited to specific offences such as wildlife trafficking or encompassing a broader range of environmental crimes, have not taken place at this stage. European Commission’s experts participated in this Expert Group meeting and the Commission continues to address this matter in close coordination with EU Member States. The objective is to efficiently coordinate and identify key priorities and guiding principles in view of upcoming discussions at the Conference of the Parties in October 2026. Member States are actively involved in this process. The objective is to achieve alignment with the Union’s policy objectives and legal framework. During the above-mentioned Expert Group meeting, the Commission and several Member States engaged with other UNTOC Parties to explore potential synergies and identify elements of future convergence. Channels of communications with international partners remain open for further liaising. The coordination ahead of the Conference of Parties will be essential to enable effective outreach and coalition-building with like-minded partners.
